judgment_text:
Prayer in OSA 193 of 2019: Appeals under Order XXXVI Rule IX of O.S. Rules read with Clause 15 of Letters Patent against the fair and decretal order dated 07.08.2019 passed in A. No. 1192 of 2019 against A. No. 7256 of 2018 in O.P. No. 891 of 2015 and consequently allow the reliefs sought for in A. No. 1192 of 2019 in O.P. No. 891 of 2015 on the file of this Court.

Prayer in OSA 194 of 2019: Appeals under Order XXXVI Rule IX of O.S. Rules read with Clause 15 of Letters Patent to set aside the order dated 07.08.2019 in Appl No. 693 of 2019 in O.P. No. 891 of 2015 and consequently dismiss A. No. 7256 of 2018 in O.P. No. 891 of 2015.

The Judgment of the Court was delivered by

M.M. Sundresh, J.:— The specific case of the first respondent in both the appeals is that they are the owner of the land and, therefore, if the pending application under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1966 (for short ‘the Act’) is decided one way or the other, the same will have a bearing on their title. After the filing of the appeals, much water has flown under the bridge. In the original petition filed under Section 34 of the Act, an order was passed in the Application No. 6642 of 2019 in O.P. No. 891 of 2015, dated 15.10.2019, which is extracted hereunder:—

“This application is filed to permit the applicant/third party to intervene in the Original Petition O.P. No. 891 of 2015. I heard the learned counsel for the applicant/third party and the learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondent in the O.P.

2. Both the petitioner in O.P. No. 891 of 2015 and the respondent in the said O.P. filed affidavits relating to this application through their respective authorized signatories.

3. Upon examining the said affidavits, the learned counsel for the applicant submitted on instructions, that the applicant is satisfied with the averments therein and is agreeable to the application being disposed of by recording the terms of the said affidavits. The learned counsel for the petitioner and the respondent in the O.P. are also agreeable to this course of action.

4. Accordingly, this application is disposed of in terms of the affidavit dated 04.10.2019 filed on behalf of the petitioner and the affidavit dated 14.10.2019 filed on behalf of the respondent. Both the said affidavits shall form part of the order.

5. The order in the application is without prejudice to the rights of the contesting parties in the O.P. as against each other.

6. List the Original Petition on 08.11.2019 at 2.15 p.m. along with A. No. 6816 of 2019 and A. No. 2795 of 2019.”

2. Thus, the grievance of the first respondent has been sufficiently satisfied. Accordingly, the appeals stand disposed of. We make it clear that the disposal of the appeals will not stand in the way of the first respondent to work out the remedy in the event of any breach of the order passed aforesaid. No costs. Consequently, connected C.M.P. Nos. 17683 and 17686 of 2019 is closed.
